summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease, chronic hepatitis C, and high-grade osteosarcoma of the left tibia was admitted for her fourth cycle of doxorubicin and cisplatin chemotherapy, complicated by a painful sickle crisis in her shoulders. Her chemotherapy was delayed one day to optimize pain control with IV hydromorphone, after which she completed treatment with minimal nausea due to scheduled antiemetics. She received one unit of packed red blood cells for chemotherapy and sickle-related anemia, and was managed for hypomagnesemia and hypokalemia secondary to cisplatin nephrotoxicity, with initiation of oral supplements at discharge. Thrombocytosis was noted but deemed reactive. GERD symptoms were better controlled on pantoprazole, leading to discontinuation of ranitidine and calcium carbonate. She recovered well, transitioned to oral pain medication, and was discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up, Neupogen injections, and continuation of supportive medications.
problems: Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
